Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.
Summary: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service today announced that weather permitting, prescribed burns will begin Saturday, Oct. 17, at Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge. Burning operations are expected to take three to five days.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside, the useful question is observational: use the report as a planning signal — precipitation, wind, and visibility change what is safe and worth noticing. Keep the publisher’s claims provisional until you read the original. If you go out, pair the story with current Dashboard readings rather than the headline alone.

item.title: NASA’s SpaceX CRS-35 Launch Jellyfish
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: NASA.
Summary: The exhaust plumes of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying the company’s Dragon spacecraft are seen illuminated by sunlight against the predawn sky during the launch of NASA’s SpaceX CRS-35 mission, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, as seen from Cocoa Beach, Florida. The light makes the plumes look like a jellyfish in the sky.

item.title: Transporter-18 SmallSats Encapsulation
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: NASA.
Summary: Three NASA-supported small spacecraft, shown along with many commercial payloads, before being encapsulated in a SpaceX Falcon 9. The rocket launched the payloads into low-Earth orbit at 11:32 a.m. PDT Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026, as part of the company’s Transporter-18 mission from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.
